page.layout: One column of running text, with a centred title (heading) at the top and a verse poem below it, set in italic lines. No margin notes. Printed page number at top right.

main_text.head: DE AMORE COSSÆI ET ARETES.
main_text.p:
Quo te sub antro, quo nemore auio
Æstus leuantem frigore languidos
Cossæus aspexit profanis
Cerui oculis, Arete, insolentem?

Tu cura es illi, seu rusco dies
Arridet ortu, seu medio dies
Incandet æstu, siue cælum
Nox tacitis operit tenebris.

Tu si vocaris per iuga Caucasi
Te belluosi, torrida solibus
Per tesqua Maurorum, per æquor
Puppibus indomitum sequetur.

Non tecta tectis, prædia prædijs,
Aurúmve stratis cogere montibus,
Non curat Eoum decoris
Oceanum spoliare gemmis.

Non otiosa lentus inertia
Vitæ fugacis ver breue carpere,
Somnóque iucundo molestas
Ægri animi releuare curas.

Vnam irretorto lumine te videt,
Vnam inquieta follicitudine
Te spectat absentem, inuocatque:
Te Dominam veneratur vnam.

page.notes: Verse is set in italic with long s; the transcription above renders the long s as a plain s per the rules, and some letters in the scan are damaged (e.g. "rusco" in line 2 of the second stanza, "Æstus" and "tesqua" read with some doubt). Line-ending "Quo" printed as a large woodcut-style initial Q with "uo" following; reading "Quo" assumed. "Cossæus" and "Arete" as printed. Signature "F. iiij." at the foot right, rendered as printed; the scan reads "F. iiij" with the last j shown as ij-like form, so treat as [?] if in doubt. Ink and paper damage present at the top of the page; the word "Arete" in the title line is partly obscured.
